Heard learned counsel Sri S.M.Kalwad for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel Sri H.R.Gundappa for respondent Nos. 2 and 3.
2.

This petition is filed by the petitioners seeking for a declaration that the acquisition proceedings initiated by respondents vide Annexure-C, in respect of land of the petitioners have lapsed in terms of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short the Act, 2013).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is the case of petitioners that they are joint owners of land bearing Sy.No.360/1/B +1 c,
measuring 1 acre, 27 guntas and Sy.No.399/1, measuring 5 acres, 37 guntas, situated at Betageri village of Gadag taluk.

The respondent No.1 got issued preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short the 'Act of 1894'), at the request of respondent No.2 to acquire about 127 acres, 26 guntas belonging to the petitioners and others for the purpose of construction of houses in Gadag.
4. Thereafter, in pursuance to the 4(1) notification issued under the Act of 1894, 6(1) notification came to be issued by respondent No.1 on 09.02.1993.
This being the state of affairs, the award came to be passed on 04.02.1997 by the respondent No.1, fixing the market value of Rs.45,000/- per acre.

5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that though the land was acquired in the year 1992, award came to be passed in 1997 and even after a lapse of 14 years from the date of award, neither the physical possession of the land has been taken nor the land is utilized for the purpose for which it was acquired.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 6.

It is further contended by learned counsel for petitioners that they raised a dispute based on which a reference application under Section 18(1) of the Act of 1894 was made the Court for determination of proper market value, by which respondent No.1 referred the matter to the reference Court under Section 18(2) of the Act of 1894.

The reference Court at the instance of the petitioners enhanced the compensation amount at the rate of Rs.2,17,372/- per acre with all statutory benefits in LAC No.45/1997.
7.

Being aggrieved by the judgment rendered in the LAC Court, respondent No.3 preferred an appeal in MFA No.7028/2003, so also the petitioners preferred MFA.Crob.No.147/2004 seeking to set aside the order and for enhancement of the compensation respectively.

This Court in the Division Bench judgment, dismissed the appeal of respondent No.3 and allowed the cross objection of the petitioners and enhanced the market value at the rate of Rs.4,42,875/- per acre with all statutory benefits.

Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the appeal, the respondent No.3 took up the matter before the Hon'ble Apex Court seeking for reduction of the award amount and SLP (Civil Appeal No.27804 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 to 27813/2008), Hon'ble Apex Court reduced the compensation to Rs.2,95,500/- per acre.

Therefore, the same has attained the finality after the Hon'ble Apex Court Sri Ranganath Yallappa Jadhav vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123968159/
3 has reduced the compensation with respect to the land in question.
8.

sentences.text: It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the acquisition proceedings initiated by respondent No.1 is bad in law and so also the purpose and scheme for which the acquisition was initiated has not been fulfilled or initiated and therefore, the acquisition itself would lapse as it is not utilized for the purpose for which the land is acquired, so also learned counsel for the petitioners contends that under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013 the proceedings would lapse as more than five years prior to the commencement of physical possession an award is passed and till date, the physical possession has not been taken.
On these grounds, he contends that the acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondent No.2 requires to be declared as lapsed due to non compliance of the Act of 2013.

9. Per contra, learned counsel Sri H.R.Gundapa representing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and learned HCGP for the State vehemently contend that the facts on the present NC:
2024:KHC-D:9489 case is that the 4(1) notification came to be initiated on 06.02.1992.

The 6(1)
notification of the 1984 Act came to be initiated on the 09.02.1993.

Pursuant to which the petitioners along with other similarly situated persons preferred Writ Petition No.36481/1993, in which an interim order of stay came to be passed, due to which the acquisition proceedings could not be pursued, further for payment of compensation, an award could not be passed.
Thereafter, in the year 1995, the writ petition came to be disposed of.

Pursuant to which, on 14.07.1997 the award was passed by the respondent No.1 and on 21.04.2004 the respondent Nos.2 and 3 have taken possession of the lands of the petitioners and others involved in the acquisition proceedings.

further contends that admittedly, the acquisition proceedings ended up in the reference Court at the request of the petitioners and the reference Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.2,17,372/- per acre from Rs.45,000/- per acre, which was taken up in appeal by the respondent No.3 and so also by the petitioners herein in cross objection, wherein this Court vide Division Bench order enhanced the compensation in favor of NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 the petitioners and dismissed the appeal of the respondent No.3 and increased the market value at the rate of Rs.4,42,000/- per acre with all consequential statutory benefits.

11. This order came to be challenged by respondent No.3 before the Hon'ble Apex Court in SLP Civil Appeal Nos.27804 to 27813 of 2008, whereby the Hon'ble Apex Court put a quietus to the litigation by reducing the compensation amount to Rs.2,95,500/- per acre.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is the contention of learned counsel Sri H.R.Gundappa that the petition would not be maintainable and would not be entitled to any favorable order for the reason that Section 4(1) and 6(1) notifications have been issued simultaneously and thereafter due to the intervention of this Court in the writ petition, by granting an interim order, award could not be passed and ultimately after disposal of the writ petition award came to be passed on 14.02.1997 and thereafter the possession of the lands have been taken from the petitioners.
Learned counsel also contends that petition would not fall within the category of Section 24(2), where the award has been made five years or more prior to the commencement of the Act.
As in the present NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 case, the award is passed soon after the disposal of writ petition which was disposed of in the year 1995 and an award was passed on 14.02.1997.

Learned counsel further contends that apart from these aspects, petitioners herein challenged the matter before the reference Court and the reference Court had enhanced the compensation,
which was further enhanced by the Division Bench of this Court.
Therefore, when he sought for higher compensation, the petitioners cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed on these grounds.
contends that the question of acquisition proceedings lapsing would not arise in the present facts and circumstances of the case.
Accordingly, the petition deserves to be dismissed.
14. I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the respondents.

15. Learned counsel for the petitioners relied on the Judgment in the case of Govt. of NCT of Delhi vs. Manav Dharam Trust and another, reported in AIR 2017 SC 2450 so also in the case of Muniswamy vs. State of Karnataka and another, reported in 2016(3) AKR 111 in support of his case.

Whereas, the learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 3 relied on the Judgment passed by the Constitution bench in the case of Indoor Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal and Others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129.

entities.text:
Indoor Development Authority vs.
Manoharlal and Others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said Judgment the Constitution bench at paragraph No.366 held as under:
"366.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, we answer the questions as under:
366.1.
Under the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) in case the award is not made as on 1-1-2014, the date of commencement of the 2013 Act, there is no lapse of proceedings.
Compensation has to be determined under the provisions of the 2013 Act.

In case the award has been passed within the window period of five years excluding the period covered by an interim order of the court, then proceedings shall continue as provided under Section 24(1)(b) of the 2013 Act under the 1894 Act as if it has not been repealed.
The word "or" used in Section 24(2) between possession and compensation has to be read as "nor" or as "and".

The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, compensation has not been paid then there - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 is no lapse.
Similarly, if compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken then there is no lapse.
The expression "paid" in the main part of Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act does not include a deposit of compensation in court.

The consequence of non- deposit Sri Ranganath Yallappa Jadhav vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123968159/
5 is provided in the proviso to Section 24(2) in case it has not been deposited with respect to majority of landholdings then all beneficiaries (landowners) as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the 1894 Act shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.

entities.text: Sri Ranganath Yallappa Jadhav vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case the obligation under Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has not been fulfilled, interest under Section 34 of the said Act can be granted.
Non-deposit of compensation (in court) does not result in the lapse of land acquisition proceedings.

In case of non-deposit with respect to the majority of holdings for five years or more, compensation under the 2013 Act has to be paid to the "landowners" as on the date of notification for land acquisition under Section 4 of the 1894 Act. 366.5.

In case a person has been tendered the compensation as provided under Section 31(1) of the 1894 Act, it is not open to him to claim that acquisition has lapsed under Section 24(2)
due to non-payment or non-deposit of compensation in court.
The obligation to pay is complete by tendering the amount under Section 31(1).

The landowners who had refused to accept compensation or who sought reference for higher compensation, cannot claim that the acquisition - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act.
The proviso to Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is to be treated as part of Section 24(2), not part of Section 24(1)(b).

The mode of taking possession under the 1894 Act and as contemplated under Section 24(2)
is by drawing of inquest report/memorandum.

Once award has been passed on taking possession under Section 16 of the 1894 Act, the land vests in State there is no divesting provided under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act, as once possession has been taken there is no lapse under Section 24(2).

The provisions of Section 24(2) providing for a deemed lapse of proceedings are applicable in case authorities have failed due to their inaction to take possession and pay compensation for five years or more before the 2013 Act came into force, in a proceeding for land acquisition pending with the authority concerned as on 1-1-2014.
The period of subsistence of interim orders passed by court has to be excluded in the computation of five years.
366.9. Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act does not give rise to new cause of action to question the legality of concluded proceedings of land acquisition.
Section 24 applies to a proceeding pending on the date of enforcement of the 2013 Act i.e. 1-1-2014.

It does not revive stale and time-barred claims and does not reopen concluded proceedings nor allow landowners to question - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 the legality of mode of taking possession to reopen proceedings or mode of deposit of compensation in the treasury instead of court to invalidate acquisition."
16.

Learned counsel has taken me through the relevant paragraphs of the Judgment stated herein supra, more specifically, paragraph No.366.3, wherein it is held that if compensation has been paid,
Sri Ranganath Yallappa Jadhav vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123968159/
6 possession has not been taken then there is no lapse.

entities.text: Ranganath Yallappa Jadhav vs The Land Acquisition Officer on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, in paragraph No.366.5 it is very clearly held that where the landowners, who had refused to accept the compensation or who sought for reference for higher compensation cannot claim that the acquisition proceedings had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

Further in paragraph No.366.8, it is held that wherever the authorities have failed to do their action to take up possession and pay compensation for five years or more before the Act came into force i.e., as on 01.01.2014 and during the period of subsistence of interim orders passed by the Court has to be excluded in the computation of five years.
17.

On considering the present facts and circumstances of the case, apparently the action of the respondent authorities in the entire acquisition proceedings of 4(1) and 6(1)
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9489 notifications and the award being passed is lesser than five years.
When the compensation has already been paid/ deposited before the Court
, the question of lapse of the acquisition proceedings would not arise.
Thirdly, the petitioners' are landowners, who sought for higher compensation cannot seek to claim that the acquisition proceedings have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.

Under the circumstances, taking all these into consideration, the proceedings initiated by the 1st respondent authority does not fall within any of the category to be declared, as lapsed, as canvassed by learned counsel for the petitioners.

So also the petitioners are not able to show before this Court as to any violations made in the procedure to be followed as per the old Act or the new Act to fall within the category of the lapse of acquisition proceedings.
18. Petition is devoid of merits.
Accordingly, I pass the following order:
ORDER Petition is dismissed.
